cards.explanation: The answer is the roaring of the sea. Jesus says the nations are “…bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.” (Luke 21:25) So up in the sky there are signs, and down on the earth the water is making a whole lot of noise. My mixer on high speed has never made anybody that nervous.

The answer is True. Jesus says men “…will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” (Luke 21:26) That “for” ties the two together in His words. This is a heavy part of the passage, friends.

The answer is the Son of Man. That's Jesus describing His own coming. He says they will see “…the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” (Luke 21:27) When Jesus says Son of Man, He means Himself (Mark 2:10).

The answer is to stand up and lift up your heads. Jesus says, “When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads…” (Luke 21:28) Right after talking about men fainting from fear, He tells His listeners to stand tall. I love that. That's a posture I wish my flour sacks had.

The answer is redemption. Jesus says to lift up your heads “…because your redemption is drawing near.” (Luke 21:28) That's the reason He gives for looking up instead of down. He doesn't say it's something to dread. It's something drawing near.

The answer is summer. Jesus says, “When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.” (Luke 21:30) Nobody has to explain it to you. You look at the tree and you just know.

The answer is the kingdom of God. Jesus says, “So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.” (Luke 21:31) Leaves show summer is close, and these things happening show the kingdom of God is close. Same kind of seeing, friends.

The answer is His words. Jesus says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.” (Luke 21:33) Even heaven and earth don't outlast what He says. That's why I take His words so seriously, and why the ovens stay ready.

The answer is the worries of life. Jesus says, “But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life…” (Luke 21:34) Worries of life are right there in His list, next to the other two. I think a lot of us know that one well.

The answer is suddenly like a snare. Jesus says, “…that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.” (Luke 21:34) A snare doesn't send a warning before it catches. Then He adds, “For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.” (Luke 21:35)

The answer is False. Jesus says, “For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.” (Luke 21:35) It isn't only about the people of Jerusalem. It reaches everyone who lives on the earth.

The answer is stand. Jesus says to pray “…that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.” (Luke 21:36) Stand is His word. After all the fainting and fear, He's talking about standing before Him.

The answer is on the Mount of Olives. The writer says, “Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.” (Luke 21:37) Temple by day, Mount of Olives by night. That's a steady routine, friends.

The answer is all the people. The writer says, “And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.” (Luke 21:38) All of them, and early. I can barely get to my own ovens that fast.
